substances.name: Hydrochloric acid (HCl)
substances.description: Strong acid — fully dissociates in water. Found in stomach acid.

substances.name: Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)
substances.description: Battery acid. Industrial uses. Extremely corrosive.

substances.name: Vinegar (CH₃COOH)
substances.description: Weak acid — only partially dissociates. 5% acetic acid solution.

substances.name: Lemon juice
substances.description: Contains citric acid. Sour taste = proton donation to taste receptors.

substances.name: Orange juice
substances.description: Citric and ascorbic acids give it pH ~3.5.

substances.name: Black coffee
substances.description: Mildly acidic due to organic acids formed during roasting.

substances.name: Rainwater
substances.description: Slightly acidic because CO₂ dissolves to form carbonic acid.

substances.name: Blood
substances.description: Tightly regulated at pH 7.35–7.45 by carbonate buffer system.

substances.name: Baking soda (NaHCO₃)
substances.description: Weak base used in cooking. Reacts with acids to release CO₂.

substances.name: Household ammonia
substances.description: Cleaning agent. Weak base, partially ionizes in water.

substances.name: Bleach (NaOCl)
substances.description: Disinfectant. Highly alkaline. Never mix with acids — produces Cl₂ gas!

substances.name: Drain cleaner (NaOH)
substances.description: Lye. Fully dissociates. Saponifies fats, clears drains.
